analysis.title: Securitization Weekly Overview: Dem rule, growth, rates: downside risk up, upside risk down
key_insights: Democratic gubernatorial gains in Texas, Georgia and Ohio add uncertainty to U.S. data center investment. The three states hold 130.5 GW of planned and under-construction capacity, 37.7% of the 345.9 GW U.S. pipeline, including 93.1 GW in Texas, 19.8 GW in Georgia and 17.6 GW in Ohio.

BofA does not expect a near-term capex cliff. Projects under construction or with committed power have substantial sunk costs and should be relatively insulated. The risk is concentrated in later phases and announced projects that still need power, transmission, permits or incentives.

The election matters less for 2027 construction than for how much of today's pipeline converts into 2028-30 spending. BofA expects higher costs, longer timelines and some relocation, not an AI investment bust.

The pipeline can adjust four ways: build as planned with more local contribution, modify or phase projects, move incremental investment to other states (Indiana, Louisiana, Utah, West Virginia, Wyoming), or delay or cancel later phases. Relocation protects the level of national capex better than its timing.

Meta's Richland Parish campus in Louisiana is the example of the local bargain: expansion to 5 GW and more than $50bn of investment, 7,500+ peak construction jobs, more than $1.6bn of contracts with Louisiana businesses and more than $1bn of local infrastructure.

Nominal capex can rise at first if hyperscalers fund more generation, transmission and substations. The macro drag appears when higher costs and longer lead times push spending into later years or cause marginal phases to drop out.

BofA keeps its 10yr Treasury forecasts of 5.0% for YE26 and 4.75% for YE27. It lowers the probability of the 10y above 6% upside scenario (tied to 7-9% nominal GDP growth) and raises the probability of a decline to the 4.25% area.

BofA believes risk assets are bottoming and credit spreads are near the wides. It keeps an agency MBS overweight and finds non-QM AAA and selected data center ABS/CMBS attractive. It likes adding high quality corporate and CRE CLO floaters.
ABS spread widening since Q3 end exceeds hyperscalers, IG and CMBS on a percent-change basis. BofA reads this as typical ABS selling to raise cash in a downturn, which creates relative value.
With the 10y at 4.86%, slightly above the 4.75% area BofA expected as a near-term destination, BofA sees less room for further rate declines and expects rates to turn higher from here.

For securitized credit, BofA argues for selectivity over avoidance. Existing and construction-stage assets with secured power may gain value if new supply is harder to deliver, while speculative outer-year projects deserve more scrutiny.

Agency MBS: basis tightened 4bp WoW. BofA keeps the basis overweight and expects the year-end rally to continue. October prepayment speeds fell 9%. 2026 YTD net issuance is $170bn, up 37% from $124bn, against a FY26 forecast of $206bn.

Non-agency MBS: weekly issuance about $3bn, YTD $234bn, a post-GFC record. NQM AAA at 140, Jumbo FCF at 145, HELOC/CES at 140bp. October CPR: Jumbo 2.0 at 7, Non-QM at 12, CES/HELOC at 18. 14 deals were called in October with about $4.1bn pre-call balance.

CMBS: BofA is neutral on private label and agency CMBS. Conduit spreads drifted wider, LCF AAA at T+82. About $170bn of private label CMBS is expected through year end. Blackstone priced the year's largest CMBS deal at $3.34bn, a multifamily portfolio.

ABS: issuance is $347bn YTD with $407bn expected for the full year. Spreads should stay rangebound with a wider bias. BofA expects weaker consumer credit performance, with conditions more supportive in 1H27.
CLO: spreads were unchanged, AAA at S+120 and BB at S+775. Data center term loans held prices better than bonds despite a $500mn loan BWIC on Thursday after the midterms.

Securitized gross issuance is $2.21tn YTD, up 13% YoY, and net issuance is $455bn, up 19%. Agency MBS gross rose 17% to $1.18tn, non-agency RMBS 29% to $234bn, ABS 5% to $347bn. CLO gross fell 19% to $141bn.

Corporate supply is the bigger competitor for capital. IG gross issuance is $1.94tn, up 26%, and net issuance is $901bn, up 75%. Treasury net issuance fell 21%. Leveraged loan gross and net supply fell 10% and 41%.

Weekly returns were a rates rally led by duration, not credit. Munis returned +1.21%, 10yr UST +1.17%, 7-10y AAA CMBS +1.11%, agency MBS +0.97%. HY corporates (+0.11%), AAA CLO (+0.10%) and BB CLO (+0.08%) lagged, and the S&P 500 fell 4.74%.

Spread per unit of spread volatility (5-year lookback): CCC HY corporates rank first at 9.3, all leveraged loans at 9.0. Loans and CLOs rank at the high end, which BofA reads as a relative value advantage for long holding periods.

Spread basis levels: AAA ABS 12bp over 1-3yr AA corporates, 7-10yr AAA CMBS minus 5bp vs AA corporates, AAA CLO 27bp over the IG index, BBB CMBS 548bp over BB HY, agency MBS minus 1bp vs 3-5yr AA corporate.

Week-over-week spread moves: LCF Jumbo 2.0 AAA tightened 15bp to 145, CMBS AAA (10y) widened 5bp to 85, CMBS BBB- (10y) widened 40bp to 525, CMBX 18 BBB- tightened 56bp to 837, CDX HY widened 3bp to 359, CDX IG unchanged at 62.

risk_factors: Political resistance to data centers over electricity costs, grid investment, water use, tax incentives and permanent job counts.
Higher infrastructure costs, longer permitting and interconnection timelines, and relocation gaps could cut the 2028-30 conversion of the pipeline into construction spending.
Interconnection positions, substation engineering, permits and fiber cannot move with a campus, so relocation restarts much of the development process.
Speculative outer-year data center projects that depend on future power, incentives and approvals.
Heavy IG corporate issuance ($1.94tn gross YTD, up 26%) competes with securitized products for fixed-income capital.
Weaker consumer credit performance in ABS until 1H27.
Limited primary conduit CMBS activity is clouding price discovery and conduit spreads are drifting wider.
Credit stabilization is less complete: HY, AAA CLO and BB CLO returns lagged in the week's rate rally.

tension_points.bull_case: Projects under construction have committed power and sunk costs. Hyperscalers can absorb infrastructure costs, fund generation, share benefits locally, phase projects and relocate to receptive states, so nominal investment can even rise at first and the 2027 AI investment story stays intact.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher costs, longer permitting and interconnection timelines, relocation gaps and lower returns could delay, downsize or cancel later phases, cutting the conversion of the announced pipeline into 2028-30 spending.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Evidence that hyperscalers can convert the pipeline into 2028-30 construction at the same pace, which would restore the above 6% 10yr scenario, or evidence of widespread delay and cancellation of later phases in Texas, Georgia and Ohio.

tension_points.bull_case: With the 10y at 4.86%, above the 4.75% area, BofA sees less room for further declines and expects rates to turn higher from here, keeping YE26 at 5.0%.
tension_points.bear_case: Lower growth risk raises the probability of a 10y decline to the 4.25% area while the 7-9% nominal GDP, above 6% yield tail narrows.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A 10y yield moving toward 4.25% would favor the downside scenario, and a rapid conversion of the data center pipeline would favor the above 6% tail.
